messages:
maria_support: Customer ABC reports intermittent JSON mode parse failures when consuming streaming responses. They see Python JSONDecodeError: 'Extra data' and TS runtime errors like 'Unexpected token' only on high-concurrency requests.

customer_abc: repro attached — using our Node client 0.12.1. Happens ~1 in 200 streamed responses. No errors in plain text mode, only in json mode.

maria_support: Pasted raw stream from the customer's proxy (note chunk boundaries):

```
chunk 1: 39\r\ndata: {"type":"response","payload":"{\"items\":[{\"id\":\"u1\",\"text\":\"Hello\\
W"}
chunk 2: 25\r\ndata: "orld\"}]}"}\n\n```

maria_support: You can see the JSON string contains an escaped newline (\\n) that gets split across the chunk boundary, resulting in an invalid escape ("\\\nW" / "orld\\\"}]" ). Parser fails when it tries to decode the first chunk as independent JSON.

jason_backend: Thanks — looks like the customer's proxy is framing by arbitrary chunk sizes (HTTP/1.1 chunked). Our JSON-mode streaming consumer assumes each "data: " line contains a complete top-level JSON value or ndjson entry. If the server embeds nested JSON strings that include escapes, split chunks can leave the line syntactically invalid when buffered naively.

eli_sdk_ts: Repro steps for TS SDK: use fetch with keepalive + readableStream reader, pipe chunk to textDecoder, push each 'data:' line to JSON.parse immediately. On my local run, I can recreate by forcing fetch response body to return 2 tiny Uint8Array pieces mid-escape. Minimal repro: 

```
// pseudo-TS repro
const parts = ["data: {\"x\": \"a\\","n\"}\n"]; // split escape sequence
// feed parts to parser that splits on '\n' and immediately JSON.parse each data payload
```

sam_qa: I verified Python sdks (py-client 0.17.x) do something similar — the stream->line parser treats each '\n' terminated frame as JSON without validating that it represents a full top-level object when nested escaped strings exist.

jason_backend: Root cause hypothesis: our streaming helper treats each "data: ...\n" chunk as atomic and calls the JSON-mode deserializer immediately. When an escape sequence for a string is split across underlying TCP/chunk boundaries, intermediate frames are not valid JSON. We need to change the parser to buffer until a valid top-level JSON can be decoded or use a streaming-safe state machine for string escapes.

eli_sdk_ts: Quick mitigation patch I tested locally: attempt JSON.parse(payload) and on SyntaxError, append next incoming 'data:' payload (with a small cap) and retry until parse succeeds or cap exceeded. Works for simple splits. Patch for TS SDK: attempt to decode; if fails and payload starts with '{' or '"', buffer and continue.

jason_backend: For Python client, similar approach. Sam, can you help validate with backpressure (don't let buffer grow unbounded)? Also add a max buffer bytes telemetry event so we can detect abused streams.

sam_qa: On it — will run fuzz harness that randomly splits within escape sequences and non-latin unicode codepoints too. I'll attach failing cases.

deploy-bot: New branch created: sdk/stream-buffer-fallback-1769, CI queued.

maria_support: Action items for support: 1) Ask customer to upgrade to patched prerelease when available; 2) As interim, recommend toggling to text mode + post-process; 3) Share workaround curl reproduction: the following simulates bad chunking:

```
# simulate a server that splits an escape mid-sequence
(echo -ne "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n4\r\ndata\r\n9\r\n: {\"a\": \"x\\\"\r\n5\r\n\nworld\r\n0\r\n\r\n"; sleep 1) | nc -l 8080
```

maria_support: I'll escalate this as P2 and schedule a hotfix for both TS and Python streaming parsers. Noting customer impact: intermittent parse failures causing 502-like behavior downstream.

customer_abc: thanks for quick triage. we'll try the temp workaround and stand by for the prerelease. :thumbsup:

jason_backend: I'll open the PR and tag the release notes. Also adding a test that randomly inserts chunk splits inside escape sequences and emojis.

maria_support: Closing loop — will follow up once QA confirms and we have a build. Thanks everyone.
